claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Two major Kyiv bridges hit in Russian attack, mayor says: The reported strikes come a day after Ukraine launched its largest recorded drone attack on Russia since the start of the war, according to Moscow.
- Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.
- Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive': Pakistan's ex-prime minister, who has been in prison since August 2023, says he has been denied justice.
- Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
- California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face attack: Attorney General Rob Bonta alleges OpenAI misled and endangered the public
- Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed: Professor Michael Freeman tells BBC Newsnight that he believes the convicted sex offender's injuries are consistent with a homicide.
- Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children: The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.
- Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
- Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run: The US vice-president tells Fox News that when he makes a decision to run or otherwise, he will "be all in on whatever that decision is".
- Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead: The shootings in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng highlight South Africa's struggle to curb violent crime.
- Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction: The French film star was due to start an appeal trial after being found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a Paris set.
- Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations: British singer Raye lands 11 nominations while Dolly Parton is recognised two months after her death.
